dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef001 n is the type of n-by-n real matrices, with both indices in Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the type of R, Rinv, the two inverse-residual matrices, and the final matrix equality, all of size r-by-r where r = k.val + 1.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef002 m n is the type of m-by-n real matrices.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes A, dA, and Q into m-by-r real matrices, where r = k.val + 1.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef003 n is the n-by-n identity matrix I_n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies I_r in the hypothesis R Rinv = I_r and in the conclusion's left-hand side I_r - Q^T Q.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef004 n A B is the usual product AB of two n-by-n real matrices.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the hypothesis as R Rinv = I_r and the conclusion's right-hand side as (Rinv^T E) Rinv.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: For A,dA in R^{m x r} and R in R^{r x r}, LocalDef005 A dA R is the left-associated matrix expression E = (((R^T R - A^T A) - A^T dA) - dA^T A) - dA^T dA.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the central r-by-r residual E occurring between Rinv^T and Rinv on the conclusion's right-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef006 A B is ordinary compatible rectangular real-matrix multiplication AB.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets Q R, A^T A, A^T dA, dA^T A, dA^T dA, and Q^T Q as standard matrix products.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: For Q in R^{m x r}, LocalDef007 Q is I_r - Q^T Q.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is exactly the left-hand side of the asserted conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef008 A is the transpose A^T of a square matrix A.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It turns Rinv into Rinv^T in the conclusion and R into R^T inside the residual.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: For A in R^{m x r} and R in R^{r x r}, LocalDef009 A R is R^T R - A^T A.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the first difference in E before the three additional cross and quadratic dA terms are subtracted.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef010 A is the transpose A^T of a rectangular matrix.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies A^T, dA^T, and Q^T in all Gram and cross products.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Eq expresses exact equality of two terms of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Both hypotheses and the conclusion are exact matrix equalities, not approximate relations.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite type of natural-number indices strictly less than n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The binder k selects an index with k.val < n, and all matrix row and column index sets are finite.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.val
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin.val returns the underlying natural number of a bounded finite index.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the column and square-matrix dimension r = k.val + 1.

dependency_coverage.meaning: HAdd.hAdd invokes the addition operation supplied by the relevant heterogeneous-addition instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the supplied instances it computes natural-number addition in k.val + 1 and pointwise matrix addition in A + dA.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.add

dependency_coverage.name: Nat

dependency_coverage.name: Real

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd

dependency_coverage.name: instAddNat

dependency_coverage.name: instLENat

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatNat

binders: A bounded index k in Fin n; write j = k.val and r = j + 1.
Real matrices A, dA, and Q in R^{m x r}.
Real square matrices R and Rinv in R^{r x r}.
conclusions: I_r - Q^T Q = Rinv^T (((R^T R - A^T A) - A^T dA) - dA^T A - dA^T dA) Rinv, where the residual inside the parentheses is parsed left-associatively as (((R^T R - A^T A) - A^T dA) - dA^T A) - dA^T dA.
mathematical_definitions: j = k.val and r = j + 1; because k is in Fin n, j < n and hence 1 <= r <= n <= m.
I_r denotes the r-by-r identity matrix.
All additions and subtractions are entrywise, all transposes are ordinary matrix transposes, and all products are standard compatible real-matrix products.
Define E = (((R^T R - A^T A) - A^T dA) - dA^T A) - dA^T dA. The conclusion is I_r - Q^T Q = (Rinv^T E) Rinv.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every pair of natural dimensions m,n with n <= m, every index k < n, and r = k + 1, let A, dA, and Q be m-by-r real matrices and let R and Rinv be r-by-r real matrices. If Q R equals A + dA exactly and R Rinv equals the identity matrix exactly, then the orthogonality residual of Q satisfies the exact identity I_r - Q^T Q = Rinv^T (R^T R - A^T A - A^T dA - dA^T A - dA^T dA) Rinv, with the displayed subtractions evaluated left-associatively.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: If n = 0, Fin n has no element k, so the part of the proposition quantified over k is vacuous.
For n > m there is no proof of the required hypothesis n <= m, so the original implication has no nonvacuous instance for those dimensions.
The column dimension is restricted to r = k.val + 1, hence 1 <= r <= n <= m; the statement does not directly quantify over an arbitrary independent column dimension.
Rinv is not definitionally declared to be the inverse of R; the only encoded inverse condition is the right-inverse equality R Rinv = I_r.
No orthogonality assumption on Q, triangularity assumption on R, rank or nonsingularity assumption on A, or smallness assumption on dA is encoded.
The name dA does not impose perturbative semantics: dA is an arbitrary real matrix of the stated dimensions.
The proposition contains no norms, inequalities, error bounds, tolerance constants, existential witnesses, or computed floating-point quantities; every relation is an exact matrix equality.
